items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1958-06-19, 20
items.q: And Baby Lovett was playing with us.

ctx.x: I thought Pensacola Kid was a pianist. No, he was a violin.

Never did play piano. He was a cat with a violin. I don't know, he might have could play piano, but I never did know him as a piano player. Well, Finney's telling him, I got this boy a job, Pensacola Kid, Clarence William, and Bunk Johnson. And Baby Lovett was playing with us. We let him have Baby and we took another drummer. Took little Jack Hine, that was Baby's friend. So they all went down and worked at this house together. They had a nice band. We could be on playing, you know, at night. Where were they…
What was the place? Huh? What was the place called where they worked? You know one name. Or house, wasn't it?

items.title: Charlie Love Interview, 1960-05-10
items.q: We had a big orchestra used to rehearse every Sunday. We just rehearsed over to them. And we'd invite all the musicians to that rehearsal, you know, a bunch of men. Every Sunday, there was Baby Lovey.

ctx.x: Yeah. He played by Bronk Johnson playing the trumpet. And Harry Walker in Alexander. Well, they had some different bands around there. You know, they all played the Red Book. We was all connected together, you see. We had a big orchestra used to rehearse every Sunday. We just rehearsed over to them. And we'd invite all the musicians to that rehearsal, you know, a bunch of men. Every Sunday, there was Baby Lovey. he was a drummer. He was in Kansas City now, with Lee's band. And they had some bands around there,…
